doc.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Being both a musician and a physician
summary: He describes how musicians and doctors each wondered about his commitment, which proved no impediment.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Were you known amongst your colleagues as — well gosh how do I say it — a little different, being that you had this other part of your life?

I think on both sides. Initially very early on some musicians, knowing that I was a physician and I was either studying to become a psychiatrist or after I’d actually become a psychiatrist, might say, “well gee, how serious is this cat about music?” And some doctors, not knowing me, might wonder well, “how committed is he to the practice of medicine if he’s out there playing jazz in these clubs and making these albums?” But anybody who’s gotten to know me has quickly understood how committed I am to both fields and how seriously I take them both. So it’s really never been an impediment.
